title: Reviewer Agent: Separate Builder from Marker

questions.question: Why cannot the builder reliably grade its own work?
options: Acceptance is necessary but not sufficient; problem fit and handoff readiness need a different role
It simply runs out of tokens partway through the diff and cannot finish reading its own proposed changes
It loses its authentication session before it can read the verification report back
The underlying model refuses any request that asks it to grade its own prior output
questions.explanation: The gap between builder and reviewer is where reliability lives; acceptance only proves a weaker version.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the five rubric dimensions?
options: Problem fit, since the rubric asks whether the change solved the task as stated
Scope discipline, since the rubric asks whether edits stayed inside the contract
Inference latency, a cost the five scored rubric dimensions never mention at all
Verification quality, since the rubric asks whether acceptance proved the real goal
questions.explanation: The five are problem fit, scope discipline, assumptions, verification quality, handoff readiness.

questions.question: What does role separation require?
options: A different system prompt and different inputs; the same model can play both roles if posture changes
A completely different underlying model, since the builder and reviewer are never allowed to share one
Different physical hardware, since the reviewer must run on an isolated machine
A brand-new account, since role separation is enforced entirely at the account level
questions.explanation: Discipline is in posture and inputs, not in the model identity.

questions.question: What score turns a reviewer run into a hard fail, per the lesson?
options: Any single rubric dimension scoring 0 is an automatic hard fail
A total under 5 of 10 is a hard fail; under 7 is a soft fail
A total below 8 out of 10 is a hard fail; below 9 is a soft fail
There is no fail threshold; every run needs a human tie-break
questions.explanation: The lesson says the rubric totals out of 10: a run below 7 is a soft fail, a run below 5 is a hard fail.

questions.question: What is the reviewer forbidden from doing, per the lesson?
options: Reading the builder's feedback log before writing its report
Scoring more than one rubric dimension in a single review pass
Patching the diff; it only writes a report for the next turn
Running the acceptance command again to double-check the result
questions.explanation: The lesson says the reviewer reads the diff, state, feedback, and verdict, and writes a report, but does not patch the diff; mixing roles defeats the gap.

questions.question: How does the lesson distinguish the verification gate from the reviewer?
options: The gate runs before the builder starts; the reviewer only runs on request
The gate is optional; only the reviewer is required before a merge
The gate scores 0-2 per dimension; the reviewer only returns pass or fail
The gate checks deterministic facts; the reviewer makes qualitative calls
questions.explanation: The lesson says the gate checks deterministic facts (did acceptance run, did rules pass, did scope hold) while the reviewer makes qualitative judgments (was this the right work, is it documented, is the handoff usable).
